new_statements.quote: 筆者の観察によると、チャック語の声調は低調と高調に大別できる注78。(77) a. V(低調): 母音はややながめに発音され、ピッチは相対的にひくい。 b. V́(高調): 母音はややみじかめに発音され、ピッチは相対的にたかい注79。[…] 注78 したがってチャック語では「声調」とはかんがえずに、たかい調値が「ある」か「ない」かで区別できる「アクセント」とかんがえることもできる。
new_statements.translation: According to the author's observations, the tones of Cak can be broadly divided into a low tone and a high tone [fn. 78]. (77) a. V (low tone): the vowel is pronounced somewhat long and the pitch is relatively low. b. V́ (high tone): the vowel is pronounced somewhat short and the pitch is relatively high [fn. 79]. [...] fn. 78: Accordingly, for Cak one could also, instead of treating this as 'tone', regard it as an 'accent' distinguished by whether a high pitch value is 'present' or 'absent'.

Surrounding section read (pp. 242-247, 251-252): sec. 2 p. 221 gives the syllable template (C)V(F)/T with tone an obligatory constituent; 6.1 reviews Löffler 1964 (Leichtton/Schwerton), Bernot 1967 (t…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Cak is described as a lexical tone language: every syllable ((C)V(F)/T) carries one of two tones, high (marked) vs low (unmarked), contrasting in open, nasal-final and glottal-final syllables, in mono- and polysyllables, in all combinations; Huziwara notes the privative H-vs-zero character would also permit an 'accent' analysis but gives no positional rule. No word stress is described anywhere; the only prominence asymmetry mentioned is the reduced /ə/ minor syllable of sesquisyllabic words (Huziwara 2015 p. 13; 2019 (1d)) and Bernot 1967's per-tone intensity correlates (moyen-haut 'attaquée avec force', moyen-bas 'sans intensité particulière').
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any source examined.
new_statements.exceptions: Tone: high tone is rare on /ə/ (fn. 79); two tone-dissimilation sandhi rules turn one of two adjacent high tones low around specific function morphemes (sec. 7.4, pp. 251-252); Bangla loans show no tonal tendency (6.3.2). None concern stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Statements concern lexical tone per syllable in citation forms of words (mono- to heptasyllabic examples, secs. 6.2.1-6.2.4); phrase-level sandhi treated separately (sec. 7). Variety: Baishari-dialect Cak of the Chittagong Hill Tracts, Bangladesh.
new_statements.identity_note: Huziwara's descriptions are of the Baishari dialect of Cak as spoken in the Chittagong Hill Tracts, Bangladesh (Naikhyongchari dialect and the Sak varieties of Rakhine, Myanmar differ mainly in segmental phonology; Huziwara 2019 says the tone system is shared across Cak/Sak varieties). Bernot 1967's notes are on Cak of the CHT (Bandarban area) recorded 1950s-60s through a Marma interpreter. All = Glottolog chak1270.

sources.locator: sec. 6.2 筆者の観察, (77) and footnote 78, p. 243 (p. 27); syllable template sec. 2 p. 221
sources.note: No word-stress section. Sec. 6 (pp. 242-247): two tones, low (unmarked; vowel somewhat longer, pitch relatively low) vs high (acute; vowel somewhat shorter, pitch relatively high); fn. 78 p. 243: the system could instead be regarded as an 'accent' distinguished by presence vs absence of high pitch. Summarises Bernot 1967's tone-cum-intensity description (75) p. 242. Sec. 7.3 vowel weakening a->[ə] before clitics; 7.4 two tone-dissimilation rules (H+H -> one becomes L) for certain function morphemes. Disyllables show all tone combinations (6.2.2).

sources.citation: 藤原敬介 2014. ルイ祖語の再考. 京都大学言語学研究 33. hdl:2433/196280
Bernot, Lucien 1967. Les Cak: contribution à l'étude ethnographique d'une population de langue loi. Paris: Éditions du CNRS. Appendice I 'Notation du Cak', pp. 227-229.
sources.note: No positional stress. Describes three Cak tones in open syllables each with an intensity correlate: 'ton moyen-bas.. la syllabe prononcée sans intensité particulière', 'ton moyen-haut à voyelle longue sous lequel la syllabe est attaquée avec force', 'ton bas, à voyelle brève.. syllabe prononcée avec force et terminée par une faible occlusion laryngale' (p. 228-229); tones noted via a Marma interpreter.

sources.note: English phonology summary (1a-f), p. 494: syllable C1(C2)(C3)V1(V2)(C4)/T with tone obligatory; '/ə/ can occur only as the first member of sesquisyllabic words'; 'There are two contrastive tones, the high tone (marked with the acute accent) and the low tone (unmarked).' Nothing on stress.
